prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1219; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received from the insured's side for a sideswipe that occurred while the other vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will route through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the first notice of loss and the description of the lane change. The account is consistent with the damage pattern noted on the intake form.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It places the claimant's vehicle in the affected lane at the time of impact and records statements from the responding officer that match the reported sequence.

Entry 4: Photos of both vehicles received. The damage to the claimant's rear quarter panel and door lines up with the contact area described by the other driver.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same account of the lane change as in the first notice. Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force on the loss date with no lapse.

Entry 6: Two independent witnesses were interviewed. Both confirm the sideswipe happened as described and that the claimant was seated in the vehicle throughout.

Entry 7: Appraisal of the vehicle is complete. The repair scope fits the impact described, and no prior damage to this vehicle appears in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 8: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of this type, and the initial treatment followed a standard course.

Entry 9: Prior records show a minor strain in the same knee area several years ago, which resolved completely with no ongoing complaints noted at the time.

Entry 10: Claimant's account has been consistent across every conversation, including the recorded statement taken through counsel. No changes to the sequence of events have been raised.

Entry 11: Treatment frequency has tapered as the claimant's condition improved, with follow-up visits now spaced out and discharge expected based on the current notes.

Entry 12: File is ready for evaluation of the injury and property damage components. Coordinating with counsel on the bodily injury demand and the repair authorization.
